biography.plain_text: Mark Dennis Brunsvold is an American medical-device entrepreneur who co-founded Parcus Medical, a maker of orthopaedic sports-medicine implants. He previously built Machined Metals, a precision manufacturer later acquired by Arthrex. After Parcus was acquired by Anika Therapeutics, Brunsvold returned to company-building with Future Micro Mold, which makes precision components and tooling for medical-device developers.

long_biography.plain_text:
Precision engineering preceded Mark Brunsvold's move into surgical products. At Machined Metals he developed contract-machining capability that drew Arthrex's interest; after the acquisition, he oversaw production for the orthopaedics group. In Wisconsin he joined colleagues to launch Parcus, producing anchors and other equipment used in shoulder, knee and hip procedures. Its operations later moved to Sarasota, and a listed healthcare group purchased the business in 2020.

He remained with the acquired unit before creating a new workshop devoted to extremely small moulds. Future Micro Mold combines tooling, machining and product-design work for device manufacturers. That return to factory-level problem solving continues a career spent making demanding surgical designs practical to produce.
